features.feature_value: Bad language strongly drove pair evaluation.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states profanity/bad language was the main factor when evaluating the pair.

features.feature_value: Passed posts based on not being outrageous; impact was harshness/profanity rather than what it implied.
features.evidence_span: "It was a lot the harshness of the post not what it was implying"
features.rationale: They distinguish tone/harshness (and lack of profanity/outrageousness) from the intended implication.

features.feature_value: More likely to remove when a post didn’t add anything conversationally (emotion-only without context).
features.evidence_span: "didn't really add anything to a conversation"
features.rationale: They use content usefulness/context as the deciding criterion, specifically contrasting with emotion-only posts.

features.feature_value: Looked for swear words/cursing that wasn’t helpful or inherently political.
features.evidence_span: "swear words or cursed just for the sake of cursing"
features.rationale: They describe profanity as a cue for unhelpful/non-meaningful content rather than evaluating ideology alone.

features.feature_value: Belief in a professionalism standard for political accounts influenced decisions as a pair.
features.rationale: They connect their moderation/keep-remove judgment to professionalism expectations in political speech.

features.feature_value: Vicious/threatening tone and major cussing were key signals; also reflected on whether it aligns with partisan thinking.
features.evidence_span: "How vicious a post was. Did it sound threatening? Was there major cussing."
features.rationale: They list threat/viciousness and cussing as concrete determinants for their pair evaluation.

features.feature_value: Applied the same moderation standard to both posts; compared tone/seriousness/targets to avoid viewpoint bias; handled profanity/strong criticism differently from personal attacks and protected-category targeting.
features.evidence_span: "apply the same moderation standard to both posts independent of the political position"
features.rationale: They describe an explicit pair-comparison rule aimed at consistency and anti-bias, with sub-rules based on tone/targets.

features.feature_value: Rejected both if any cursing/foul language; allowed if somewhat civil.
features.evidence_span: "If there was cursing or foul language, then I rejected both posts."
features.rationale: They provide a clear threshold-style criterion linking profanity to reject/allow for both items.
